title: They walked with Him.
paragraphs:
They walked with Him.
They heard every word.
They saw the blind see, the dead rise, demons tremble.
And they still didn’t understand Him.
That’s the part most people skip over.
The men closest to Jesus—His chosen disciples—were not clear, confident theologians walking in perfect revelation. They were confused. Repeatedly. Deeply. Sometimes painfully.
And if you’re honest… so are you.
Because the confusion wasn’t intellectual. It was spiritual.

They weren’t just misunderstanding information.
They were resisting a mission that didn’t match their expectations.
They thought they knew what the Messiah would do.
They were wrong.

They expected a throne.
Jesus carried a cross.

They expected Rome to fall.
Jesus talked about dying.

They expected power.
Jesus kept talking about surrender.
And every time He told them plainly, they struggled to receive it.
In Matthew 16:21–22, it says:
“From that time Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things… and be killed, and on the third day be raised.”
Read that again.

He didn’t hint.
He didn’t speak in riddles.
He told them directly.
And what did Peter do?
He pulled Jesus aside and rebuked Him.
Rebuked Him.
The disciple correcting the Savior.
That’s not just confusion—that’s resistance dressed as loyalty.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Their confusion wasn’t because Jesus was unclear.
It was because they were committed to a version of Jesus that didn’t exist.

A conquering king without a suffering servant.
A crown without a cross.
Glory without repentance.
Sound familiar?
In Luke 18:31–34, Jesus lays it out again:
“Everything that is written about the Son of Man… will be accomplished… He will be delivered over… mocked… flogged… killed…”
And then it says:
“But they understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them.”
Hidden—not because God is cruel, but because their hearts weren’t aligned with what He was revealing.
They were still holding onto ambition.

Who would be greatest?
Who would sit at His right hand?
Even at the Last Supper—hours before the cross—they were arguing about status.
God saw it.
You knew.
They followed Jesus, but they didn’t surrender to Him.
That’s the tension.
And that’s where many people are right now.

You listen.
You agree.
You even believe parts of it.
But the moment Jesus’ mission confronts your desires—your control, your plans, your pride—you hesitate.
Because the real Jesus doesn’t just save you.
He breaks you first.
Look at Mark 8:34–35:
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me. For whoever would save his life will lose it…”
That was the mission.

Not domination.
Not comfort.
Death to self.
The disciples didn’t reject Jesus outright.
They just kept trying to reshape Him into something easier to follow.
And that’s far more dangerous.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
Everything changed after the resurrection.

After the cross shattered their expectations…
After the empty tomb proved He was telling the truth the whole time…
Their confusion turned into conviction.
Peter—the same man who rebuked Jesus—stood boldly and preached:
“Repent… for the forgiveness of your sins…” (Acts 2:38)

No more mixed message.
No more self-centered ambition.
Because now they understood:
Jesus didn’t come to fit into their story.
They were being invited into His.
And His mission was always this:

Sin had separated you from God.
You could not fix it.
No amount of effort, religion, or morality could erase it.
So Jesus came—not to improve you—but to rescue you.

He lived the life you couldn’t live.
Died the death you deserved.
Rose again to offer you life you didn’t earn.
That’s the Gospel.

Not comfort.
Not self-help.
Not inspiration.
Redemption.
So here’s the real question:

Are you confused…
Or are you resisting?
Because there’s a difference.

Confusion can be healed.
Resistance has to be surrendered.
One version of your future keeps trying to shape Jesus into something that fits your life.
The other bows, repents, and lets Him completely rewrite it.
Only one leads to life.
Say it plainly.
“I’ve been following my version of Jesus.”
Let that come out.
And if you know someone who is comfortable with a version of faith that never calls them to surrender—send this to them.
Not to argue.
To wake them up.
You’ll need it again when your old mindset tries to come back.
And if you’re ready to stop misunderstanding Jesus and start walking in what He actually came to do—there’s more waiting for you:
